messages:
jax: Heads-up — noticed a regression in the Console inspector panel after last night's rollout. Opening the inspector now spikes main-thread CPU and LCP for the panel from ~800ms to ~2400ms on staging. Repro: open Account > Deploys > click any trace inspector.
anya: Ugh. Saw a couple similar reports from support. Any bundle size diffs in the canary?
jax: Yes — quick `sourcemap-extract` shows the new vendor chunk for inspector (+450KB gzipped) and a new large module named `devtools-lite` got in. Network waterfall shows parse/compile on main thread ~200–300ms.
leo: Do we have telemetry for first contentful paint / interactive on the panel route? I can pull charts.
sam k: I ran a quick trace in staging and saw a lot of repeated `measureTelemetryInit()` calls from the telemetry client when opening multiple panels — looks like eager init is happening per-panel instead of shared.
anya: That could explain main-thread churn. Did the telemetry client change in the same PR?
jax: Yep — PR #4281 replaced the lazy telemetry shim with a direct import to simplify the rollout UX for rollouts team. The idea was to reduce flicker, but maybe it pulled in too much.
leo: On it. Querying perf metrics now: `SELECT percentile(lcp_ms, 95), count() FROM panel_loads WHERE route = 'inspector' AND env = 'staging' SINCE 6h` gives 95p LCP jumping from 900ms -> 2300ms right after that deploy timestamp.
sam k: Also seeing KV-cache misses spike for requests hitting `/api/panel/meta` around the same time — routing policy tweak yesterday redistributed affinity across nodes, maybe cache locality got worse. That would increase network fetches and parse work.
jax: Good catch. Which routing change? The one that weights eu region higher for canary traffic?
sam k: Yes — we changed routing weights to prefer eu for 10% of canaries; seems like many panel loads got routed to cold nodes without warmed kvcache.
anya: So two plausible contributors: bigger vendor chunk (parse time) + increased backend latency/cache misses. Which is bigger?
leo: From telemetry breakdown, main-thread JS parse time accounts for ~60% of the extra latency; backend RTT added ~300ms on avg. So bundle/import explosion is the larger factor.
jax: Can we quickly rollback the direct telemetry import in the inspector bundle (lazy-load it) and revert the router weight for canary to previous? I'd prefer a quick canary rollback of the telemetry import first since it's local to the frontend.
sam k: I can flip the routing weight back in routing-config and redeploy the router policy, takes ~5m to propagate.
anya: I'll open a quick patch to re-lazy-load telemetry (wrap in dynamic import) and push a canary. Something like:```js
// before: import {initTelemetry} from 'redwood-telemetry'
// after:
let initTelemetry;
async function ensureTelemetry() {
  if (!initTelemetry) {
    initTelemetry = (await import('redwood-telemetry')).initTelemetry;
  }
  return initTelemetry;
}
```
jax: Perfect. Also let's add a temporary client-side experiment that defers parsing heavy devtools modules until the user expands details. That should reduce initial parse.
leo: I'll queue the telemetry query dashboards to show breakdown by chunk, so we can watch the gzipped delta and parse cost in real time.
sam k: ops-bot, can you create an incident with priority P2 and link the rollouts PR + routing change?
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-134 (P2) — linked PR #4281, routing-config change 2026-03-20T03:12Z, assigned to eng-platform.
anya: Rolling patch out to canary now, will post canary URL in 5m.
jax: Thanks. After we stabilize, follow-ups: 1) add chunk size budget CI for inspector route, 2) telemetry client needs single shared init across console, 3) add kvcache warmup for canary nodes when routing weights change.
leo: Adding those to backlog and tagging owners.
sam k: For the short-term rollback plan: if canary shows improvements, we revert telemetry import in stable and revert router weight tweak.
anya: Canary looks much better — 95p LCP drops to ~950ms. Rolling to stable now.
jax: Nice. Keep monitoring dashboards for 1h and if KPIs hold, close incident. Thanks team :thumbsup:
